title: Type-strict bounded Firefox/X11 terminal receipt validation

human_actor.role: Product Owner, Code Owner and rights holder
human_actor.identity_proof_boundary: Repository and platform records attribute the directive to the named account context; they are not biometric or universal identity proof.

tools_and_adapters: focused Python and JavaScript terminal checks
artificial_cognitive_actor.identity_and_observation_limits: The local executor has no Firefox runtime. Real Firefox/X11 evidence is therefore kept separate and bound only to GitHub Actions runs on their exact source head and tree.

human_contributions.description: Directed realization of the universal terminal pattern in a Firefox browser and required visible, repository-native execution rather than an Atari-only theoretical result.
Required the Firefox terminal bridge and sender protection to remain fail-closed while being re-bound to the current materialized pull-request head.

artificial_cognitive_contributions.description: Bound the first failed Firefox/X11 trace step to its current head, identified JSON string identity comparison as the false HOLD cause, and preserved prior-head evidence as non-current provenance only.
Strengthened Xvfb receipt validation so JSON strings compare by value while Boolean receipt fields remain type-strict and fail closed.
Ran the declared tool-cache gate, focused terminal test bundle, JavaScript syntax checks, deterministic XPI packaging, and repository-integrity materialization.

joint_components.human_part: product direction, safety constraints, and review-bound delivery intent
joint_components.artificial_cognitive_part: exact-head diagnosis, type-safe repair, test execution, packaging, and evidence preparation

outputs.self_binding_rule: The future Git commit and tree containing this work-unit file bind its exact bytes; no impossible in-file self-hash is claimed.
